title: Programmable all-to-all entangling gates for cavity-coupled atoms
authors: Angus Crookes, Ben Yuen, Angela Demetriadou
abstract: Fault tolerant quantum computers greatly benefit from having both high fidelity entangling gates and a non-local qubit connectivity. However, most entangling gates for neutral atoms are local, requiring separated atoms to be moved using optical tweezers to yield entanglement between them. Here, we design a high fidelity Mølmer Sørensen-like entangling gate between neutral atoms coupled to a photonic cavity, enabling a programmable all-to-all connectivity through the shared cavity coupling. The gate is both robust to changes in cavity photon number, and enables selective entanglement between any subset of separated atoms through local laser addressing. This eliminates the need to physically move atoms to perform the gate, and therefore motional errors and erasure are suppressed. Using experimentally realistic parameters we demonstrate gate fidelities exceeding $F > 0.99$, with higher fidelities achievable through optimal control of the pump amplitudes.
summary: This paper presents a method to achieve high-fidelity, all-to-all entangling gates for neutral atoms using a shared photonic cavity. By leveraging the cavity mode, the gate eliminates the need for physically moving atoms, thereby suppressing motional errors. The resulting gate is robust to photon number fluctuations and demonstrates fidelities exceeding the threshold for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a method for creating high-fidelity, programmable all-to-all entangling gates between neutral atoms without requiring physical movement (shuttling) of the atoms.
main_result: The authors successfully designed a Mølmer-Sørensen-like gate using a shared photonic cavity that achieves fidelities exceeding 0.99, enabling connectivity between any subset of atoms.
method: The gate is derived by analyzing the system Hamiltonian, adiabatically eliminating an upper atomic level, and applying the Rotating Wave Approximation to yield an effective Mølmer-Sørensen Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system consists of neutral atoms configured in a three-level Lambda ($\Lambda$) scheme coupled to a photonic cavity mode. The dynamics are modeled using the full Hamiltonian, which is then simplified to an effective Hamiltonian governing the gate operation.
key_observables: Gate Fidelity ($F$), entangled state fidelity ($\left|\psi(T)ightangle$), and the ability to selectively entangle subsets of atoms.
important_parameters: Gate time ($T$), cavity quality factor ($Q$), coupling strengths ($g_0, g_1$), and pump amplitudes ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: Key approximations include the adiabatic elimination of the upper atomic level and the application of the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level diagram, compare gate fidelities using full vs. approximate Hamiltonians, and show how fidelity depends on initial photon number, coupling ratios, and pump amplitudes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system and the problem (local vs. all-to-all gates) to deriving the effective Mølmer-Sørensen Hamiltonian, demonstrating its robustness, and finally analyzing the dependence of fidelity on various experimental parameters.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a major bottleneck in quantum computing hardware by providing a mechanism for long-range, high-fidelity entanglement generation that bypasses motional errors inherent in physical atom shuttling.
